We built it for the challenge “Build a Jr. Astronaut Mission Trainer.” Players create a cadet profile and fly four progressive missions: the International Space Station, a Moon base, a Mars outpost and deep space. Each mission includes a briefing, pre-mission learning, equipment upgrades, a launch countdown, simulated emergencies where players make decisions, and a quiz. Six connected modules share one credit wallet: Mission Control, Space Academy, Rocket Encyclopedia, Planet & Star Explorer, Performance Scoreboard and Space Live Feed, which shows NASA images and updates with their sources and dates. Space often feels distant and hard for children to approach. By turning real NASA data into missions they want to play, Cosmic Trainer makes concepts like orbits, microgravity and life support exciting, and helps inspire the next generation of space explorers.
details:
What it does and how it works
Cosmic Trainer (Junior Astronaut Trainer) is a game-style web app where young students train as astronauts while learning real space science. Players create a cadet profile and fly four progressive missions: the International Space Station, a Moon base near the lunar south pole, a Mars outpost at Jezero Crater, and deep space near the asteroid belt. Each mission follows the same steps: briefing, pre-mission learning, equipment hangar, launch countdown, journey emergencies, a destination task and a six-question quiz. Players decide how to respond to simulated emergencies such as solar array power failure, communication blackout or water-system malfunction. Wrong choices explain the correct concept instead of just penalising the player.

The app has six modules that share one credit wallet: Mission Control, Space Academy (15 lessons with quizzes), Rocket Encyclopedia, Planet & Star Explorer, Performance Scoreboard and Space Live Feed. A searchable glossary is available from every screen. Credits earned from quizzes and missions are spent on equipment upgrades that unlock harder missions.

NASA data and resources used
Real NASA photographs from the NASA Image and Video Library appear throughout, with credits. The Space Live Feed uses NASA APOD for a daily feature and NASA DONKI for space-weather events, and it links to NASA’s official live streams. ESA and ISRO resources supplement the feed. Every feed item shows its source, its original date and a label (RECENT, DAILY FEATURE or ARCHIVED), so an old photograph is never presented as new or live.

Benefits and intended impact
Space science often feels distant and hard to approach. Cosmic Trainer turns real NASA data into missions children want to play, so they learn concepts such as orbits, microgravity, radiation, communication delay and life support by using them. It needs no installation, so it can be used in classrooms and at home. Our aim is to inspire more young people to explore space science and to show them where the real data comes from.

Tools and technologies
HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS and JavaScript (React and React Router), with Recharts for progress charts and Framer Motion for animations. Player progress is saved in the browser.

What makes it creative
It combines a game (launch countdowns, emergencies, upgrades) with verified science, rather than a plain quiz site. Challenges are decisions with consequences, not just multiple-choice trivia, and the scoreboard rewards learning and improvement, not only rankings.
